title: Pinned Horizontal Gallery
summary: A gallery section pins to the screen while the reader keeps scrolling down, and that vertical scroll slides a row of six project panels sideways, with a hairline progress bar and a counter tracking the position.
useWhen: architecture or interiors practice showing a handful of projects in sequence
case study timeline that reads left to right
product range where each item needs a wide frame
replacing a carousel with something that works with the scroll wheel and trackpad
techniques: section height computed from track width

whyItWorks.how: One element moves. The script sets the section height to viewport height plus the track's overflow (track.scrollWidth minus innerWidth), then on each scroll frame writes a single translate3d to the track and a scaleX to the 1px progress bar. Layout is measured on resize only.

The page keeps native scrolling. The scroll listener is passive and only queues one requestAnimationFrame, and the offset is mapped 1:1 from scroll position (--scroll-ratio: 1) with no easing or lerp, so trackpad momentum, the scrollbar, Page Down and the space bar all drive the gallery exactly.

The track and progress bar are linear on purpose because they are scroll-linked, so the reader's hand is the easing. Easing curves appear only on hover, where the frame zooms to 1.03 over 400ms and the arrow slides in over 220ms on cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1), and leave faster at 300ms and 160ms.

Each panel is a link. Tabbing to one would normally scroll the clipped stage sideways and fight the transform, so a focusin handler resets that scroll and moves the page to the vertical position that centres the focused panel. :focus-visible gets the same zoom and arrow as :hover.

With prefers-reduced-motion the section stops pinning and the row becomes a plain horizontal scroller with scroll-snap. The bar then follows the row's own scrollLeft, so position is still shown without converting vertical scroll into sideways travel.

directions.name: Editorial
directions.change: Make panels alternate between wide images and narrow text columns with a large serif pull quote, so the horizontal run reads like a magazine spread.

directions.name: Experimental
directions.change: Skew each panel slightly by its distance from the viewport centre (computed in the same frame) and set the counter in oversized type that slides with progress.

directions.name: Luxury
directions.change: Use a dark ground, widen --panel-width to 70vw, and give each frame a slow inner parallax of about 6 percent against the track so the images feel deeper than the panel.

pitfalls: Intercepting wheel events to fake horizontal scroll breaks trackpads, keyboard scrolling and accessibility tools. Let the page scroll and map position to translation.
Forgetting to recompute the section height on resize leaves either a dead scroll gap at the end or a gallery that never reaches its last panel.
Adding lerp smoothing to a scroll-linked transform makes it lag behind the scrollbar and feel detached.
Leaving focus unhandled lets the browser set scrollLeft on the sticky stage, which doubles the offset and hides the focused panel.

tunables.name: --panel-width
tunables.effect: Width of each panel. 80vw on screens under 720px.

tunables.name: --scroll-ratio
tunables.effect: Vertical pixels scrolled per horizontal pixel moved. Raise it to slow the gallery down.

reducedMotion: No pinning and no scroll-to-sideways conversion. The panels sit in a native horizontal scroller with scroll-snap, the hover zoom and arrow slide are removed (the arrow only fades), and the progress bar follows the row's own scroll position.
